resources.string: Tap “Build number” 7 times. If you can’t see it, open “Software information” first.
Open “Software information”, then tap “Build number” 7 times.
Find “USB debugging” and switch it on.

Open OkuFlow on your computer. If it cannot connect, check that USB debugging is on and allow this computer when asked. If Developer options are missing, open About phone and tap Build number 7 times.
OkuFlow shows this camera on your computer. Nothing is sent to the internet.
Plug this phone into your computer
Use a USB cable that can transfer data.
If your phone asks “Allow USB debugging?”, tick “Always allow” and tap “Allow”.
Changes apply automatically. Your phone may use a lower resolution or frame rate.
Every mode detected on this phone, including below 720p and 24 FPS.
Using a mode from More options.
Electronic stabilization can crop the image. Choose Off or Optical when using fixed-reference stabilization in OkuFlow.
When autofocus is off, focus is set to infinity for distant content.
Starts off. Use the phone light button under Camera settings in OkuFlow on your computer.
Move left for a darker image, right for a brighter image.
Ready for the USB camera connection
The camera stopped to protect the phone. Let it cool down, then choose the phone again in OkuFlow’s camera list.
Your computer is connected. Waiting for camera video.
Close other apps that use the camera. OkuFlow tries again for a short time. If the picture does not return, choose the phone again in OkuFlow’s camera list.
Turn on camera access in privacy settings or quick settings. Then choose the phone again in OkuFlow’s camera list.
This video mode is not available
Open Advanced settings and set resolution and frame rate to Automatic.
OkuFlow tries again for a short time. If the picture does not return, choose the phone again in OkuFlow’s camera list. If this keeps happening, restart the phone.
The USB camera could not start
Close OkuFlow Camera and open it again. If this keeps happening, restart the phone.
